newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says inflation target too low.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says inflation target too low.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong recommended on Friday that the island's cabinet raise its 1997 target for consumer price growth to 3.3 percent from the current 3.0 percent.
"The cabinet's target is too low," Sheu told reporters.
He said the 3.0 percent target, announced by the cabinet on Thursday, would require the central bank to tighten monetary policy and risk slowing Taiwan's economic recovery.
"Taiwan's economic recovery is still not too strong, so it is unsuitable to tighten monetary policy at this point," Sheu said.
He said the cabinet was considering his suggestion to raise the inflation target to 3.3 percent to bring it closer to the central bank's own forecast of 3.31 percent.
Taiwan's consumer price growth in 1996 was 3.07 percent.
